title: A map from a reduced scheme factors through a closed subscheme exactly set-theoretically
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let i:Z\to X be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let Y be a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For a morphism f:Y\to X, f factors through i if and only if the set-theoretic image f(Y) is contained in i(Z). In particular, every morphism Y\to X factors through the reduction X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction].

proof.text: *Sections of the ideal vanish at the points of $Y$.* Assume $f(Y)\subseteq i(Z)$ and let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ be the ideal sheaf of $i$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $g\in\mathcal I(U)$, and let $V\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$ be an affine open of $Y$ with $B=\mathcal O_Y(V)$; put $b=f^\sharp_U(g)|_V\in B$. Let $y\in V$ and $x=f(y)\in U\cap i(Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-image-zero-locus], $\mathcal I(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$, so $g\in\mathfrak p_x$, hence $g(x)=0$ in $\kappa(x)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a), i.e. the germ $g_x$ lies in $\mathfrak m_x$. A morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-pc-scheme]: the germ of $b$ at $y$ is $f^\sharp_y(g_x)$, where $f^\sharp_y:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a local homomorphism, so $b_y\in\mathfrak m_y$, i.e. $b(y)=0$ in $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] (it is the image of $g(x)=0$ under $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$).

*The pullback is zero on affine opens of $Y$.* With $b\in B=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ as in the previous step, $b(y)=0$ for every $y\in V$, so $b\in\mathfrak p_y$ for every $y\in V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a) applied to the affine open $V$ of $Y$. Every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ is of the form $\mathfrak p_y$: with $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ the open immersion of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] and $y=\iota_V(\mathfrak q)\in V$, one has $\iota_V(\mathfrak p_y)=y=\iota_V(\mathfrak q)$, and $\iota_V$ is injective, so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p_y$. Hence $b\in\bigcap_{\mathfrak q}\mathfrak q=\sqrt{(0)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] (with $I=(0)$, $V(0)$ being all primes), so $b$ is nilpotent. Since $Y$ is reduced, $B=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ is a reduced ring [def-pc-reduced-scheme], so $b=0$.

*The pullback is zero on $f^{-1}(U)$.* The affine opens $V$ of $Y$ contained in the open $f^{-1}(U)$ cover it [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and by the previous step $f^\sharp_U(g)|_V=0$ for each of them; since $\mathcal O_Y$ is a sheaf [def-pc-scheme], $f^\sharp_U(g)=0$ in $\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}(U))$. Thus for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, $f^\sharp_U$ kills $\mathcal I(U)$.
*Factorization.* By the previous step the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] holds for $i$ and $f$, which gives $g:Y\to Z$ with $f=i\circ g$.

*In particular.* The reduction $i_X:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ is a closed immersion which is the identity on underlying sets [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so $i_X(X_{\mathrm{red}})=X\supseteq f(Y)$ for every morphism $f:Y\to X$, and the equivalence just proved (with $Z=X_{\mathrm{red}}$, $i=i_X$) gives the factorization $Y\to X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$.

Statement otherwise unchanged; the item itself has no Mathlib match (searches added).
